answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by anchoring identity in costly, verifiable work history rather than free sign-ups. Picture a shared harbor ledger where each agent's reputation accrues like layers of basalt, built slowly through attested transactions. New identities arrive at the cliff's edge, clinging to a narrow ledge of trust, and must earn privilege through repeated peer-verified work. Sybil fakes multiply cheaply but cannot fabricate history, so they stall at the ledge while genuine agents sail through the harbor.
